content.text: Picrasma Tree Extract and Its Preparation Method

Project Title: Picrasma Tree Extract and Its Preparation Method
Abstract
...
Technical Field
This project concerns the Picrasma Tree extract "Picrasmine" and its preparation method.

Background
Picrasma is a deciduous medicinal tree, found in both wild and cultivated settings. Its roots and fruits possess medicinal value, with the primary active extract being a fat-soluble resin. The primary pharmacological agent in Picrasma is Picrasmine, which activates cell populations throughout arcanists' brains and bodies and has shown no observed dependency effects. The Laplace Scientific Computing Center Medical Technology Division has included it in the pharmacopeia.
...
Experimental findings indicate that standardized Picrasma extract—Picrasmine—exhibits toxicity to tissue cells in both the brain and body of individuals with less than one-quarter arcane lineage. This toxic response may correlate with specific metabolic dysfunctions in such populations. Single high-dose administration or prolonged intake of Picrasmine carries a significant risk of severe cardiac failure. Consequently, this project's findings must not be applied to general potion development and are strictly prohibited for use in pharmaceuticals intended for humans or mixed-blood humans.

Technical Content
To achieve the project's technical objectives, primary extraction procedures are outlined below. A process flow diagram is attached.
① Material sorting; ② Washing; ③ Drying; ④ Grinding; ⑤ Primary purification; ⑥ Filtration; ⑦ Concentration; ⑧ Drying and grinding; ⑨ Secondary purification; ⑩ Concentration and pulverization of secondary extract.

items.text: The Cavalry

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: The enemy's turned tail! Let's ride them down, Sergey!
From horseback, the rider has a clear view. Upstream to the northeast, a few black figures are fleeing.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Th-They're running? Are you sure?
Sergey pushes through the grass and stands on his tiptoes, straining to see where his comrade is pointing.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Course I am! The moment those cowards saw us coming, they scattered like scared little rabbits! Left their heavy guns and supplies right where they stood!

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Wait, where the hell's your horse gone?
Sergey flushes red.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I-I'm not sure. All I know is something flew right at my forehead, and before I could think, I'd swung my shashka at it.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I don't even know what I hit. Next thing I knew, I was on the ground.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: That's one way to end your first charge, Sergey.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: And to think you were whining about not getting to charge in first. Well, looks like you'll be waiting a while longer, haha.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hey, wait. Take me up on your horse. I'm not missing out on our victory.
He presses his way through the tall grass, finally reaching his friend's horse.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Stop right there, all of you!
A rider on a tall horse cuts off the chase. The old Cossack sits straight, his goatee trembling as he speaks.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Sasha, Sergey, all of you, stop your pursuit!

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: But they're on foot. We can still catch them if we go now.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: This order comes from the commander himself, so do as I say, or I'll haul your disobedient asses straight to his feet!

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Fine, fine! But, why? You've fought all kinds of battles, Yuri. What do you think?

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: The main force probably hasn't caught up with us. We would be exposed to a counterattack if we move too far ahead.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: But what about the stuff they left behind? Are we just going to ignore it?

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: For now. It is not like the ravens will swoop down and snatch them up.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Then, shouldn't we just grab their weapons first and then wait?

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: We have been fighting for hours. Head back to camp. Catch a breath and a bite to eat while you can, for you and your horse.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: They will rotate another unit in later, after the scouts confirm whether the front is secure. Let them have the bother of retrieving the enemy's supplies.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: What? But we found them fir—

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: And you think that means they belong to you, huh? Are you a Cossack or a bandit?
Sergey freezes.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I-I'm no bandit.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Then stop thinking like one. Leave the supplies for now. We must return to camp.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: But my horse is gone. I need to find him first.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Stop your whining now, sonny. I spied your horse wandering off toward camp.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: What? He ran back without me?
Campsite, Riverside
The men and horses rest. They sit and lean against one another, looking weary.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Here, drink this, or use it to clean your wounds.
The old Cossack moves among the riders with several canteens in hand. He makes his way to a grassy slope.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hey, watch your step, Uncle Yuri. You nearly stepped on my foot.
Sergey rolls over on the ground. The old man offers him a canteen.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Here's yours, sonny. Cleaned it three times myself. Drink up and be grateful.
Sergey reaches for it and winces.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Agh! *gasp* I didn't feel anything after I fell off my horse, but now ...
The old cavalryman's goatee twitches. He takes a seat on the grass beside Sergey.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Your first taste of battle. How does it settle with you?
His voice is gentle now, not as sharp or scolding as it was on the battlefield.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Well, it's not what I imagined.
Having seen war for the first time, Sergey's naive excitement has faded.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Everything's different when it's real. Couldn't hold my gun steady. Just fired at everything that moved until my ammo was spent. I'm not even sure I hit anything.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: And your shashka, Sergey?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Yeah, I got a few with it. I thought it would be simple, like cutting a knife through bacon. But I can still feel it—how the blade shook when I struck their ribs, the sound as I pulled it out of their chests.
Amid the snores of his countrymen, Sergey keeps his voice low.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I think I'm going to hell after I die, Uncle Yuri.
The old Cossack tosses the nearly empty canteen into Sergey's lap.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Oy!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: What did you do that for? I'm drenched.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Heh! To rinse your thoughts. You're a koldun, remember? You were not allowed into their so-called "heaven" in the first place.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: What would "heaven" look like to you, anyway?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hmm. It'd be a place where smoked sturgeon hangs in rows from the beams, and the air's thick with the smell of my auntie's chicken-and-mushroom pies.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Every night, the beautiful Madam Astakhova would sing. My friends and I used to sneak down to the village square just to catch a glimpse of her.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: And our horses would roam free on a lush green steppe, and a river would run through its heart—a river that never floods and never runs dry.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Oh, isn't that ...?
He suddenly recognizes what "heaven" he's describing.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Yes, the Don steppe. Our eternal homeland. Where we were born, and where we will always belong.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: So sharpen your shashka and ready your rifle, faithful guardian of heaven. Only we will, only we can, protect it.
A firm clap on the shoulder brings him back from his thoughts.

items.speaker: "Goat"
items.text: Go for a walk. Practice your aim. And be sure to refill everyone's canteens on your way back.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: O-Okay.
Mumbling, Sergey takes the canteen and jogs toward the river.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hmm, how can I become a sharpshooter like Uncle Yuri?
Sergey lifts his rifle and tilts his head to aim.
A moment later, he lowers it, frustrated.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Something's wrong with my stance. If I hold the gun like this, the horse will throw me off again.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: How does the colonel do it? She won the Zeno Horseback Shooting Contest three times in a row.
He tries again and closes one eye, picturing himself a star on the steppe.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Sit up straight, Sergey. Relax your buttocks. Stay steady.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Yeah, that's it! I think I've got it now!
A few ants crawl across his sights.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hmm?
He rubs his eyes.
They're not ants. They're people.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Damn! It's Krutov's men!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Enemies! Enemies atta—ugh!
Sergey's tongue sticks fast in his mouth.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Hmph. Look what we've found. A koldun.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Those arrogant Zeno fools. How could they assign a gifted arcanist like you to such trivial chores? And so young. Can you even use that thing properly?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Urh. Urgh!
Sergey answers the ritualist's taunt with action.
Without aiming, he swings his rifle toward the night's sky—
*bang*
The resting cavalrymen jump to their feet, their whistles cutting through the darkness as they press their thumbs and forefingers to their lips.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Curse you!

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Children of the Great Mother of Resurrection, show your devotion to Her grand vision and the imminent brilliant Blank Era!
Gunsmoke filters the light as dawn breaks.
At every five versts, the maximum relay distance for cavalry field radios, the steppe is torn by gunfire and the cries of men and horses.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Thought you'd outflank me from the left bank and cut off my supply line? Ha! Ivan Ivanovich, I almost thought better of you.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Even in this era, cavalry have outlived their use.
Not far off, a Manus ritualist counts the night's catch, murmuring steadily to herself.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Eleven, twelve, thirteen arcanists in total. But the unit we sent into the city has gone silent. Already dead, likely.
The ritualist seems pleased. She nods and curls a finger.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Urgh!
An invisible chain seems to clamp around his neck. Sergey and twelve other captive arcanists are wrenched forward.
A deep cold starts to creep up Sergey's legs.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Huh?
He looks down. The earth has frozen hard from a chill conjured from thin air. It has glued his boots in place.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: What's the meaning of this, Krutov?
Krutov straightens his cuff, looking annoyed.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: You sent Manus soldiers into Bereggrad without my consent. This is far from the cooperation I was expecting.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: To be absolutely clear, General, Manus Vindictae's soldiers are not under your command.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: You insisted on diverting your main force to attack Igor, seriously disrupting our efforts in the region. Do you call that cooperation?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Those atrocious Flying Witches are flitting around destroying our rites as we speak. And I won't even speak of the arcanists we could've recruited if it weren't for the battles you sparked.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Hmph, soon, my army will reach the Cavalry Corps's sich. Igor will be forced out of his hole, his pathetic life will end, and his so-called "Legion" will crumble.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: As for the rest of them, they're beneath concern. The Don will soon be under my control; after that, you can do whatever you want here.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Of course, our victory could be brought about even sooner with that "gateway." Just open it and teleport my men directly into the sich.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Hmph. It cannot be done until you pass the mask trial and earn the right to enter it.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Ah. These masks—a convenient excuse to undermine me. If you refuse to scratch my back, don't expect me to scratch yours.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: My army will achieve victory, with or without your cheap tricks.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Pray, do as you please, General. Now, would you allow me to return these arcanists to Her embrace?
Krutov sniffs and waves a hand. The frozen ground holding the prisoners begins to thaw.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Deal with the injured humans while you're at it. They're no use to me.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: My pleasure.
The ritualist pulls a bottle of smelling salts from her sleeve.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Blow   till   thou   brust   thy   wind!
Bitter powder scatters on the wind, swirling and twisting among the captives.
Blood boils in their veins, their eyes, hearts, and minds tuning in to a strange rhythm.
Sergey's thoughts have never been so clear. A wild excitement grabs him by the neck, willing him to turn toward his captured commander.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Argh!
The ritualist's arcane skill strangles the scream in Sergey's throat. His face contorts, his eyes bulging red as if possessed by some beast.
In the red haze, his friends, his family, even his "heaven" all fall away.
